title: Independent localization formulas for both tensor-shift reassociation routes
statement: Let X be a scheme with the recorded derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] and canonical tensor shift [def-sc-scheme-canonical-tensor-shift]. Let P,T,U be K-flat sheaf complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Write Q for localization and mu for its lax monoidal tensorator, eta(V):Q(V[1]) -> Q(V)[1] for its shift comparison, and s for the first-factor tensor shift (subscripts c and d mean complex and derived). Set A=Q(P), K=Q(T), M=Q(U). Define v=(eta(P)^(-1) tensor id_K tensor id_M);(mu(P[1],T) tensor id_M);mu(P[1] tensor T,U), and c=(id_A tensor mu(T,U);mu(P,T tensor U))[1];eta(P tensor (T tensor U))^(-1). Then c is invertible. Moreover (alpha(A[1],K,M);s_d(A,K tensor M));c = v;Q(alpha(P[1],T,U);s_c(P,T tensor U)), and ((s_d(A,K) tensor id_M);s_d(A tensor K,M);alpha(A,K,M)[1]);c = v;Q((s_c(P,T) tensor id_U);s_c(P tensor T,U);alpha(P,T,U)[1]). These are separate route normalizations and assert no equality between the two complex composites.

proof.text: Convert sheaf K-flatness to the two-sided upstream quasi-isomorphism preservation condition using acyclic cones and symmetry. The Q tensorator is invertible with a K-flat factor. Hence mu(T,U), mu(P,T tensor U), their whiskered/shifted maps, and eta inverse are invertible, proving IsIso c.

Normalize the first route independently: expand c, move mu(T,U) through s_d using second-variable naturality, and use the defining first-variable localization shift square for P,T tensor U. Move eta(P) inverse through the associator by associator naturality. The lax monoidal associativity equation rewrites the resulting tensorator composite as v followed by Q of the complex associator. Functoriality gives the first displayed formula. Use the liftingIsoApp shift square of the recorded IndependentTensorShift construction and transport quotient followed by Qh to Q along quotientCompQhIso.

Normalize the second route independently: expand c and apply lax monoidal associativity at P,T,U under the shift functor. Move mu(P,T) through s_d for the fixed third factor by naturality. The first-variable localization squares for P,T and P tensor T,U rewrite the two successive shift comparisons. P tensor T is K-flat since tensoring any acyclic F with it is reassociation of (F tensor P) tensor T. Tensorator naturality in the first variable moves the localized first comparison into Q. Naturality of eta at the complex associator completes the second formula. This uses neither the complex coherence equation nor any equality of the derived routes.

theorem schemeTensorShift_localization_normalization
    (P T U : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := X.sheaf) P)
    (hT : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := X.sheaf) T)
    (hU : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := X.sheaf) U) :
    letI := schemeCanonicalTensorShift X
    letI : ∀ B : schemeDerivedCategory X, (tensorRight B).CommShift ℤ :=
      fun B ↦ Functor.CommShift₂.commShiftFlipObj (h := .int) B
    let A := DerivedCategory.Q.obj P
    let K := DerivedCategory.Q.obj T
    let M := DerivedCategory.Q.obj U
    let c := schemeTensorShiftTargetComparison X P T U
    let v := schemeTensorShiftSourceComparison X P T U
    IsIso c ∧
      ((α_ (A⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) K M).hom ≫
          ((tensorRight (K ⊗ M)).commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app A) ≫ c =
        v ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((α_ (P⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) T U).hom ≫
          (CochainComplex.mapBifunctorShift₁Iso P (T ⊗ U)
            (curriedTensor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))) 1).hom) ∧
      ((((tensorRight K).commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app A) ▷ M ≫
          ((tensorRight M).commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app (A ⊗ K) ≫
          (α_ A K M).hom⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧') ≫ c =
        v ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map
          ((CochainComplex.mapBifunctorShift₁Iso P T
            (curriedTensor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))) 1).hom ▷ U ≫
          (CochainComplex.mapBifunctorShift₁Iso (P ⊗ T) U
            (curriedTensor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))) 1).hom ≫
          (α_ P T U).hom⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧')
